raw_response:
I will still do it much like last year, because changing too much at my age is risky. On my 9.5 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize, and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around here, if wheat and maize are managed steadily and watered from the well at the key time, they bring money more safely than trying something fancy. I only finished primary school, so I do not talk big theory, but after 40 years I know where yield comes from: good seed, enough fertilizer, water at the tight time, and not being late with spraying. Fertilizer is expensive, that is true, but losing yield is more painful than spending a bit extra, so I will not cut too hard. I will use improved wheat seed, hybrid maize, and improved cotton seed if the price is not too high. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer and give one more nitrogen topdressing at greening or jointing; with well irrigation I will water about 3 times if the year is normal. For maize after wheat, I will sow quickly, use a bit heavier fertilizer than wheat, and water 2 times if rain is short. Cotton on the smaller piece takes more looking after, more sprays too, but if I keep the stand even and do not let insects get ahead, it can still give me decent cash. I watch what nearby farmers do, and my numbers are close to that, just adjusted a little so I do not starve the crop.
